summary: Hant's Harbour light on Custard's Head, Trinity Bay: a wooden tower lit in 1881 after an 1880 petition; the present square tower dates from 1957.

lens.note: Eighth order first supplied; sixth-order dioptric substituted (Inspector's report printed in 1894; LHF dates the change to 1893).

structures.note: First light on Custard's Head: wooden octagonal tower with a one-storey store attached (LHF). Height not given.
Present tower. Coast Guard list gives 8.0 m; LHF gives nine metres.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LHF). Short trail over the headland at the end of the road; no formal parking (LHF).

events.note: Petition from inhabitants of Trinity Bay for a light-house at Hants Harbor (House of Assembly entry).
Wooden octagonal tower on Custard's Head; the 1881 report says the harbour light was completed.
Argand lamp in an eighth-order lens, fixed white light (LHF).
Sixth-order dioptric light substituted for the eighth order (LHF dates 1893; the report is printed in 1894).
Listed in the Light List as square instead of octagonal (LHF).
Fixed white changed to flashing white; kerosene replaced by acetylene gas (LHF).
Present square pyramidal tower built, according to the Canadian Coast Guard (LHF).
Commercial electricity strung to the light (LHF).

corrections.proposed: Split: first wooden octagonal tower built 1881 (height not recorded); present square pyramidal tower built 1957, 8.0 m (Coast Guard list) or 9 m (LHF).
corrections.why: The 9 m height belongs to the 1957 tower, not the 1881 tower. Sources disagree on the present tower's height (8.0 m CCG; nine metres LHF).

corrections.proposed: Remove 1957 first_lit; record 1957 as the year the present tower was built (replaced).
corrections.why: The light was lit in 1881 (1882 Journal: harbour light completed; LHF gives first lit 1881). 1957 is the date of the present tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett and LHF agree the light was first lit in 1881; Wikidata gives 1957, the date of the present tower. The 1882 Journal records the harbour light as completed.
OSM's Fl R 4s is the Coast Guard's separate Hant's Harbour Breakwater Light (Fl R 4s), not this light. The main light is Iso W 6s.
The Coast Guard gives 19.8 m for the main light; LHF gives the same focal plane for 1881 to 1957. The OSM figure (4 m) belongs to another entry.

notes_for_editor: Primary checks: the House of Assembly journals (Memorial University DAI PDFs) give the 1880 petition and message, the 1880 survey, the harbour light completed by the 1881 report, the 1885 complaint (report dated 1 Jan 1886), the 1889 'good order' report and the 1893 sixth-order change. The JHA page numbers are PDF pages (pdftotext form feeds); printed page numbers differ (the 1889 Journal's printed p. 210 is PDF p. 224). OCR quirks: 'Trinitr' for Trinity, 'ancl' for and, 'tn.uch' for much, 'in· different' for indifferent, 'Hant&' for Hant's; the story corrects these in running text, and the evidence quotes keep the OCR form so check_quotes.py can find them. Not verified in a primary source: the Soper names and their dates (LHF only; the town's history page repeats LHF word for word, so it is not independent), the 1914, 1931, 1957 and 1968 items (LHF, citing the Light List and Coast Guard), and the 1893 date. The Inspector's report for 1881 is signed in OCR as 'J. T. ... EWILL'; the title and content match Nevill's other reports, so the story names no signatory. No wreck, storm or rescue was sourced for this station, so that chapter is omitted. Newspapers were not searched. Rowlett's Hant's Harbour entry (ibiblio nfle.htm) was not read, so Rowlett's dates are not checked here. Whoadana and willowtreeheritage.com were read and add nothing that LHF does not give. Wikipedia was read for leads only and is not cited. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1880 notice (JHA PDF p. 155) and message to the Legislative Council (p. 161) match the story; the 1881 sentence on the Bay Roberts Point site and the Hant's Harbour beacon light is in Inspector Nevill's report for 1880 (report heading PDF p. 805, sentence p. 808); the 1886 complaint and reply (p. 1081, OCR 'RANTS HARBOR' is the section heading) match; the 1890 'in good order and well cared for' and leaky fountain (p. 499, OCR 'Rant's Harbor') and the 1894 sixth-order dioptric substitution (p. 318) match. The Coast Guard entry (Iso W 6s, 19.8 m, 13 nm, red and white structure 8.0 m) matches. The 1886 keeper identity as W. Soper is LHF's, and the story now attributes it to LHF. The 1957 tower height is 8.0 m (Coast Guard) against nine metres (LHF), and both are kept.
